_comment: Store listing copy, in the shape the two consoles ask for. Kept as data
The App Store NAME is not the on-device name. What shows under the icon
is CFBundleDisplayName (Info.plist) / appName (capacitor.config.ts) /
app_name (strings.xml), all of which say "Doxa" since D472. This field is
the listing title only. Under the old name it read "InSight: Daily
Perspective", because plain "InSight" was already taken on the App Store on
2026-08-05 — a first-come reservation by another developer, not a trademark
matter — and that collision was one of the reasons the name moved. It now
reads the bare "Doxa" so the listing and the on-device name agree; if App
Store Connect reports it taken, the suffixed form is the fallback and
asc-push will say so (a 409 naming the attribute).
play.title is kept identical so the two stores do not silently diverge,
but it is NOT bound by that collision: Play has its own namespace, so
revisit it if Play is ever un-parked (D42).
rather than prose so scripts/check-store-listing.mjs can hold every
field against its store's character limit — both stores reject an
over-length field at the end of a long manual form, and Apple's
keywords field in particular is silently truncated by some tooling
rather than rejected.
The privacy answers are NOT here. They live in docs/SHIP-CHECKLIST.md
section 3, derived from docs/data-inventory.md, and duplicating them
into a second file is exactly the drift this repo has paid for before.
Placeholders in ALL_CAPS are owner-gated facts, same class as the
web/terms.html values check:store-copy guards.

through a file inside one workflow run, so the password never lands
in the repo or in a log.

appReview.notes:
Doxa requires an account before any question can be answered. The FASTEST way in is Sign in with Apple, which needs no email round trip.

If you prefer the email door, please use the demo account supplied above — it is already confirmed. An account created with a fresh address will be held at a "Confirm your address" screen until its confirmation link is opened, which is the app working as intended rather than a defect.

Why the account is required rather than optional (guideline 5.1.1(v)): the account is not gatekeeping a feature, it is the unit the product is about. Every screen in the app compares your own answers to other people's over time — a daily question answered by nobody in particular produces nothing the app can show back. Answers are public and attributed by design; the sign-in screen says so before anyone signs up.

Sign in with Apple, Google and email/password are all offered (guideline 4.8).

apple.name: Doxa
apple.subtitle: Answer blind, then compare
apple.promotionalText: You answer before you can see anyone else's answer — then the split appears, and you find out whether you're with the crowd or the rare side.
apple.description:
You answer blind — no counts, no comments, nothing to anchor you — and only then does the split appear.

Sometimes you're with the crowd. Sometimes you're the rare side. Either way you found out honestly, because you committed first.

— THE DAILY —
A question a day to open with, and a feed of hundreds under it. You never see how anyone voted until your own answer is locked in. The counts you then see are exact — the real split, from the very first answer.

— DUELS —
Groups and one-on-ones with people you actually know. Everyone answers the same question, every answer stays sealed until the reveal, then it all opens at once with names attached. In a 1v1 you also guess what they'll pick — call it right and the streak grows.

— THE MAP —
Every answer becomes a dot in your constellation. Four profiles — personality, politics, values and social style — fill themselves in from questions you already answered. No questionnaires, no homework. Watch yourself take shape.

— WHAT IS PUBLIC, SAID PLAINLY —
Most apps bury this in a policy and hope you don't check. Here it is up front, because it is the whole point of the app:

• Your answers are public. Anyone using InSight can see what you answered, under your display name, along with the age band, gender, city, country, education and relationship status you have filled in. That is what the app is for — it is how you see who answers like you — but it means nothing you answer here is private. Answer accordingly.
• That includes the political, personal and sensitive questions. No category is held back, and no group is too small to show: counts are exact from the very first answer, so in a small cohort a count of 1 is visibly one person's answer.
• Your display name is shown with your answers, and with any take you post. Leave it blank to appear as “Someone” — that hides the name, not the answers.
• Sealed means sealed. Duel answers are unlocked by the server at the reveal, so nobody can peek early and then play.
• Nothing here is fake. No invented users, no seeded comments, no head start on your profiles — they start empty because you haven't filled them in yet.
• An account is required, and that is deliberate: answers that belong to a phone rather than to a person cannot say anything about you, and a handset that is replaced takes them with it. Sign in with Apple, with Google, or with an email address you confirm. Nothing you answer is lost by signing in.
• Deleting your account erases your profile, your answers and your memberships.

One question. An honest answer. Then the truth about where you stand.
apple.$whatsNew: Apple REFUSES this on a first release — there is no previous version for it to be new against, and the PATCH comes back 409 naming the attribute (D74). asc-push sends it in its own request for exactly that reason, reports the refusal as a skip, and applies it on the first UPDATE. Keep it accurate here regardless; the value below is what ships the moment there is a version to be new against.
